Decisive: p^2 + 0.5*2p(1-p) = p identically, so a two-agent plurality with a random tie-break is exactly as accurate as one agent at every p. Verified to 1e-16 over 999 grid points. The marginal value of the second agent is 0.000 points, not small, and this needs no model to establish. Under a FIXED tie-break the same algebra gives p(1-p) per item, whose expectation p(1-p)(1-rho) is exactly half of the paper's Eq. 3.
